additional_info.subject: ID0433372-DC/Si-D/SA-[MP / RD 170002986]Technical Query CRM:02681000397
additional_info.body:
Hello Sadek,
From the video that the customer shared, I can see that the FC14 is blinking red. From what I know, sometimes the HMI causes a surge of current and the fuse trips.
Please check the following:
Untrip FC14 and see if it comes back to green.
If yes, then it could be that during a boot up the current requested was higher than the fuse can handle and tripped.
If this is the case, probably the HMI is the root cause. You can test by removing the 24V to the HMI here and reboot the charger:
If the FC14 is green, that means that the surge is coming from the HMI and needs to be replaced or change the position where this 24V come from. I already performed this once and changed it to FC12 but this needs to be documented if it's done.
If no, then that means a component is tripping the FC14.
Usually it's the HMI, you can test the same as above by removing the 24V and untrip the FC14 again.
If it goes to green, we have a faulty HMI
If it still is red, we need to understand which component from the 24V line is the root cause.
If it's red, please trial removing one by one from the terminal:
When you find the faulty component follow that line and check if there is any short circuit or replace it.
Since the root cause is usually always the HMI, I recommend taking a spare HMI to site in case you need to replace it.
Thank you!
Best regards,
Francisco

additional_info.subject: ID0433372-DC/Si-D/SA-[MP / RD 170002986] FC14 tripped CRM:00314000195
additional_info.body:
Dear colleagues,
I am reaching out in regards of ticket
ID0433372
for charger
170002986.
The charger shows the fuse FC14 blinking with red light. The following tests have been performed:
Pressed FC14, still red light.
Switched off and on FC12, still red light on FC14.
According to the electric schemes:
Disconnected XD21.4C, performed the procedure at point 2, still red light. 24V absent.
Disconnected XD21.A1, performed the procedure at point 2, still red light. 24V absent
With XD21.A1 disconnected, performed the procedure at point 2 and measured in XD3.9A, 24V absent. Also, PLC KF1 is switched off.
At this point, further verification could not be performed. It was proposed to measure the voltage directly on Fc14 and to switch FC14 with FC17, in order to narrow down even more the source of fault, but the technician onsite said he was not able to do it.
As per the current results, it seems that the FC14 has an issue and cannot close. It is required to order a new FC14, to replace the component and to proceed with the troubleshooting.
The spare part to be ordered is:
Please let me know once the replacement is planned, so that we can schedule in advance another remote support to proceed with the troubleshooting.

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0433372-DC/Si-D/SA-[MP / RD 170002986] FC14 tripped CRM:00314000195
additional_info.body:
Dear colleagues,
I am reaching out in regards of ticket
ID0433372.
Today we had a remote support call for charger
MP/RD 1700002986.
After last intervention, FC14 was replaced, but the error was still present on the fuse. Today we performed several tests and:
If no load is connected to FC14, the lights turn green (it was not the case last time)
IF only PLC is connected, no issue
If the 24V to the door without the HMI is connected, no issue
If the 24V to the HMI is connected, the fuses trips.
This is a quality issue of abnormal absorption from HMI, and especially when connected to FC14, the fuse trips.
As a temporary solution, we bridged the HMI 24V under FC16 instead of FC14. The 24V connection in F11-XD21.4C which goes directly to the HMI is removed, and it is bridged in F03-XD3.20D.
The HMI will need to be replaced, but it can work temporarily like this. To complete the activity, we restored the correct connection to the routers XF4 and XF3 to the LAN of the charger and the external router.
Charger is now online and working. The OCPP Backend needs to be configured, end customer needs to provide OCPP Charger ID and OCPP Backend url.
Please proceed to order the HMI and replace it.
